about: The Sketchbook brand kit: warm, whimsical, wise. Use whole files; don't edit or redraw them. To add a piece, ask for it in https://github.com/lean-software-production/brand.
rules: One idea per slide: a title, then at most one row of panels, or one bubble and one ribbon.
Characters are supporting cast: small, at the edge, doing something. Never the centrepiece.
Pictures of things beat pictures of people for explaining a step.
Only use the palette colours. Don't invent new ones.
Use everyday words; explain any jargon briefly.

pieces.about: A numbered step in one of the five main colours. Add .sk-dashed for a dotted outline, to highlight the step you're talking about. Use .sk-em for accent text.

pieces.name: Speech bubble
pieces.about: Something a person says or asks. Add .sk-tail-right to move the tail to the right.
pieces.html: “I want to learn Chapter 1 of Shape Up, while I’m driving.”

pieces.name: Ribbon banner
pieces.about: An insight or takeaway. The kicker word goes in .sk-kicker, and an icon is optional.
pieces.html: Insight: “I want to learn a book while driving.”

pieces.about: A short slate connector between steps, and the blue loop-back arrow that sits under a row of panels.

How to get the agent
to teach you anything

The learning loop

1Add sources

books, manuals, transcripts, code

2Filter + focus

use a lens: “what do I care about?”

3Create new source

pull out just the parts that matter

4Create a projection

audio summary, infographic, quiz

5Validate + iterate

teach back, quiz me, spaced repetition

Insight: “I want to learn a book while driving.”
